probes.payload: {{baseline}} AND SLEEP(5)-- -   # prepend junk>=WAF-limit before this
probes.description: WAF body-inspection-limit bypass: prepend junk data larger than the WAF's inspected window so the injection sits beyond it while the backend still parses the full body. Documented limits — Cloudflare 128KB, AWS 8-64KB, Akamai 8-128KB, Azure 128KB, Barracuda 64KB, GCP Armor 8KB. Send as a large POST/JSON body with a junk field first, the injectable param last; time-based oracle confirms.

XML decimal-entity WAF bypass: the injected value sits inside an XML request body (delivery vector — see xml_injection.json contexts) so the WAF inspects the raw bytes and never sees the keywords AND / EXTRACTVALUE / CONCAT / SELECT — each is written as decimal numeric character references (AND = AND, SELECT = SELECT). The XML parser decodes the entities before the value reaches the DB, so the EXTRACTVALUE XPATH error still leaks version(). Requires an XML-body-borne injection point.

XML hex-entity WAF bypass, time-based oracle: AND SLEEP(5) with keywords written as hexadecimal numeric character references (AND = AND, SLEEP = SLEEP). Same mechanism as the decimal form — WAF byte-matching misses the encoded keywords, the XML parser decodes them before the DB parses the query. Requires an XML-body-borne injection point (xml_injection.json is the delivery vector); confirmed by the >=5s response delay.

XML hex-entity WAF bypass, boolean form: a single quote (') plus OR 1=1 (OR 1=1) hex-encoded so the quote and keyword never appear literally in the inspected bytes. Result-set expansion vs baseline confirms. Delivery vector is an XML request body (xml_injection.json); the XML parser resolves the character references before the SQL engine parses the statement.

order_by_sink.description: Blind extraction via the ORDER BY / GROUP BY clause as the injection SINK (not column-count enumeration). Applies when the input lands directly inside ORDER BY so quote-breaking and UNION are unavailable — you cannot escape the clause, but you can substitute an expression that branches on a condition. Oracle forms: boolean-blind via a CASE that divides by zero on one branch (visible error only when the branch is taken), error-based CAST of a subselect to int, and time-based PG_SLEEP / SLEEP.

probes.description: ORDER BY boolean-blind oracle via division-by-zero: the CASE expression evaluates 1/(SELECT 0) whenever the condition is FALSE, forcing a divide-by-zero DB error. Swap 1=2 for the real condition (e.g. (SELECT SUBSTRING(version(),1,1))='1') — an error means the ELSE branch ran (condition false), a clean sort means the THEN branch ran (condition true). Confirms the ORDER BY sink is injectable when UNION/quote-break are impossible.

ORDER BY error-based extraction via CAST: casting a text subselect to integer fails and the DB echoes the offending value in the error. PostgreSQL: 'invalid input syntax for type integer'; MSSQL variant is CONVERT(int,(SELECT @@version)) -> 'Conversion failed'. Leaks version() through the type-mismatch error message.

words: invalid input syntax for type integer

probes.description: ORDER BY time-based oracle (PostgreSQL): a subselect over PG_SLEEP(5) in the ORDER BY clause delays the response by >=5s. MySQL form is ,(SELECT SLEEP(5)); MSSQL uses ,1;WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'--. Wrap in a CASE (PG_SLEEP fired only on the true branch) to turn it into a per-bit blind extraction. Last-resort oracle when no error or content differential is available.

craft_guidance: 1. IDENTIFY CONTEXT: Determine if input lands in WHERE clause, ORDER BY, INSERT VALUES, or LIMIT. Each needs different break characters.
2. DETECT DB ENGINE: Use vendor-specific errors or functions — @@version (MSSQL), version() (MySQL/PG), sqlite_version() (SQLite), banner (Oracle).
3. CHOOSE TECHNIQUE by visibility: Error-based (fastest) > UNION (data extraction) > Boolean blind (slow but reliable) > Time-based (last resort) > OOB DNS (when no output at all).
4. UNION EXPLOITATION: Find column count with ORDER BY N (increment until error), then UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,...,NULL to match. Replace NULLs one-by-one with data extraction functions.
5. BLIND EXTRACTION: Use SUBSTRING(value,pos,1) with binary search on ASCII values. For time-based, calibrate delay against baseline latency (+2s minimum delta).

6. WAF BYPASS CHAIN: Try in order — inline comments (/*!50000 SELECT*/), case variation (sElEcT), whitespace alternatives (/**/ or %0a), double encoding (%2527), concat char-by-char (CHAR(83)+CHAR(69)...).
7. FILTER EVASION: If quotes blocked, use hex (0x61646D696E), CHAR(), or numeric comparison. If spaces blocked, use /**/ or %09 (tab). If keywords blocked, use synonyms (COALESCE vs IF, CASE vs IIF).
8. OOB EXFILTRATION: MySQL LOAD_FILE+INTO OUTFILE, MSSQL xp_dirtree/xp_fileexist to UNC path, PostgreSQL COPY TO PROGRAM, Oracle UTL_HTTP.REQUEST.

9. XML-ENTITY WAF BYPASS: when the injection point is inside an XML request body (delivery vector: xml_injection.json contexts), encode SQL keywords as decimal (SELECT = SELECT) or hex (SELECT) numeric character references. A WAF inspecting raw bytes never sees the keyword; the XML parser decodes the entities before the value reaches the DB. Encode only the keywords (SELECT/UNION/AND/OR/SLEEP/quote) — the rest can stay literal.

10. ORDER BY SINK: when input lands directly in ORDER BY you cannot quote-break or UNION. Substitute a branching expression instead — CASE WHEN (cond) THEN 1 ELSE 1/(SELECT 0) END (boolean-blind via divide-by-zero error), CAST((SELECT ...) AS int) (error-based), or (SELECT 1 FROM PG_SLEEP(5)) (time-based). See the order_by_sink context.
